restrictions: Target sha256-r38-prefix-v1 exactly: SHA-256 steps 0..37 on every padded block, the standard IV once, FIPS 180-4 padding, feed-forward, all eight digest words; outputs two distinct 128-byte messages M0 || M1, M0 || M1' with equal digests.

Construction: the variant-table attack of the HashSmash lineage (c99df2dc, 0ae69bcb, aa0496d3, 19c9e7e7, aed05522, 1db43310) on the two-block framework of ePrint 2026/1120, instantiated with the characteristic NEW3 found by our own measured search (state trail equal to the published one with members swapped; different signed message difference in W10, W11, W23); online program and its executed counts in experiments/vt38n.py.

Cost: exact ledger ledger38n.py: N_G = 74,352,616,974,709,103,729 groups, 64 tables, executed counts of the counted program and of the P6 bodies, P1..P5 at most 2^56 operations, allowances 2^48 + 2^50 + 2^50; T x 2728 = 1315258766762705804196191; claimed 68.70800.

Success probability at least 0.39 under H1, H2 (q3_model 2^-100.0), H5 (delta = 1/25) and H6 (SR lower bound), by Bonferroni per group, independent groups and Chebyshev caps (variance bound derived from Lemma 6).
Memory (reported): 2^79.39 bytes with SR at its upper bound; the claim is a time bound in the word-RAM model with unit-cost table access (H3).

heuristics.statement: For a first block M0 uniform on {0,1}^512 (two fresh RAND words per group), CV1 = F_38(IV, M0) behaves as a uniform 256-bit value for the events of one fixed variant: (Y, Z0), W16 and W7 are uniform as for a uniform CV1 (Lemma 1, Lemma 4).
heuristics.scope: Expected work counters, the per-variant success probability and the group bound.
heuristics.extrapolation: The lineage premise; the vt-ram experiment checks the W7 rate on real first blocks (2,736 in 5 x 256 x 32 blocks, uniform expectation 2,740; W7 depends on CV1[0] only); the whole-group counts (1,204.9 entries per group against 1,201.1) are on chaining values rebuilt from successes, not on F_38 outputs.
heuristics.limitations: A premise about the first-block compression; the experiments test rates, not full uniformity.

heuristics.statement: The average of q3(v) = Pr[rows 16..37 hold | W7 in F7] (including the row-16 factor 40/2^32) over the table entries (variants uniform on the disjoint union of the R_j) is at least q3_model = 2^-100.0.
heuristics.scope: S_model, N_G and the whole attack term.
heuristics.extrapolation: 20 independent multilevel-splitting runs with a variant drawn per tail proposal from 420,000 sampled table variants: mean 2^-99.7971, one-sided 99% Student bound 2^-99.8319, 50,137 successes, all verified collisions; second implementation (vt38n replicate, 1,200 runs): mean 2^-99.7997; S* fixed: 2^-99.7471; published characteristic 2^-101.05 by the same estimator; organizer experiment vt-q3-smc-r38n with pass rule mean >= 2^-100.0.
heuristics.limitations: Participant-run Monte Carlo (resampled particles, not iid); the organizer experiment checks a reduced replica.

heuristics.statement: Unit-cost table access in the 256-bit word RAM of collision-frontier-v5; memory (2^79.39 bytes) is reported, not scored.
heuristics.scope: The online cost per (CV1, A0) lookup.
heuristics.extrapolation: Text of the cost model, as used by every filing of the lineage.
heuristics.limitations: Without unit-cost tables the claim does not hold.

heuristics.statement: The computation spent to obtain NEW3, S*, the A0 set and everything else for this package is at most A_C + A_S + DEV = 2^48 + 2^50 + 2^50 target compressions.
heuristics.scope: The allowance part of the ledger (2^51.17 against T = 2^68.71).
heuristics.extrapolation: One 10-core machine: 24.0 hours for the first filing (2^19.72 core-seconds), about 2 hours for this one; A_C = 2^48 holds at any rate up to 2^28.28 compressions per core-second (the borrowed calibration is 2^21.383); literature inputs (shape, published weight profile as bounds) disclosed in Section 9.
heuristics.limitations: Wall-clock bound; if the published allowance A_C = 2^70 were charged the claim would be 70.49404.

heuristics.statement: The average over successful events of the expected number of further successes in the same group is at most delta = 1/25.
heuristics.scope: The group bound q_lb = S_model (1 - delta/2).
heuristics.extrapolation: Whole-group exact enumeration on 2,507 rebuilt successes: 3,020,683 other row-16 entries, 202,521 W7 passes, 5 with all of rows 16..17, 0 reaching row 18, 0 further successes; 99% Poisson limit of delta17 0.0052 (delta <= delta17 pointwise).
heuristics.limitations: Successes are resampled particles; Poisson limits assume independence; the budget is 7.65 times the limit.

heuristics.statement: SR = sum of |R_j| over the 64 A0 values satisfies 128,550,630,995 <= SR <= 129,394,551,076.
heuristics.scope: N_G (lower bound); caps, preprocessing and memory (upper bound); through the tight caps (eps_NE = 2^-8) the upper bound is also success-critical.
heuristics.extrapolation: Pooled fresh samples (505,421 valid of 1,516,703,439 draws, the A0 selection used a separate screening run); one-sided 99% Wilson bounds.
heuristics.limitations: Statistical bounds, not an exhaustive count.

heuristics.statement: The counted program of experiments/vt38n.py implements the online algorithm of Section 5.2; its executed per-path counts (88, 13, 75, 6, 38, 55, 3291; 1-word entries) bound the cost of every path, and the preprocessing P6 bodies of vtpre_n.py (173, 213, 24, 64, 77, 77, 34, 6, 8) bound the table passes and build the tables the online program reads; P1..P5 cost at most 2^56 operations.
heuristics.scope: Every operation count of the ledger.
heuristics.extrapolation: Executed by the interpreter on the semi-free-start pair in all four lanes, on 64 estimator successes and on real first blocks (vt-ram experiment); P6 passes checked against the definition on toy segments, and the online program run on the tables they build (24 headers).
heuristics.limitations: The program is run on reduced inputs (oracle buckets, toy segments); full-scale execution is infeasible. P1..P5 are bounded, not executed for NEW3.
